# Entre-deux — proposition visuelle v1

Illustration de fiction produite avec l’outil intégré image_gen. Deux vues des extrémités d’une même créature. Anatomie proposée ; la composition ne fixe ni taille ni capacité universelle.

[Image](entre-deux-v1.png)

## Prompt

Use case: stylized-concept. Create a cinematic detailed fantasy bestiary illustration in a single landscape image with two equally sized adjacent scene panels, no lettering. Show TWO DISTANT PARTS OF ONE CREATURE, called an ENTRE-DEUX, a non-humanoid instinctive creature of spatial magic inhabiting an existing passage between a medieval watermill loading room and a fortified granary. Left panel: timber and stone watermill interior, flour dust, sacks, glimpse of mill wheel outside. Right panel: granary with stone walls and grain sacks. At each location the SAME animal has a pale pearlescent organic ring of articulated limbs and sinewy attachments physically gripping the sides and top of a doorway. Anatomy should read as a real creature, not a carved decorative arch: fleshy folded joints, taut tendons, gripping digits, slight asymmetry, coherent crown-like bodily mass around the aperture. Distinct from a spider or a protection barrier: no web, no six-legged white stone guardian above door, no stone armor. Long smooth ivory limbs hold geometrical poses, three prominent articulated limb groups around each aperture with matching poses and subtle corresponding bands of dusky violet pigmentation identifying the two parts as the same organism. The passage is the creature's own deep transparent iridescent opening, not a flat forcefield: THROUGH the left aperture we clearly see the granary; THROUGH the right aperture we see the watermill. Both doorway openings are clear and unobstructed, with restrained refractive violet rim, no magical energy vortex. One ordinary burlap grain sack is midway across the threshold, its continuation visible in the counterpart scene, illustrating the physical connection. No second full independent animal, these are two anatomical ends of one spatially distributed organism. No human characters needed. Full doorway and limb anatomy visible in both panels, consistent eye-level three-quarter perspective, warm mill light contrasted with cool granary daylight, tangible medieval textures, solemn strange beautiful neutral animal. Photoreal painterly cinematic craftsmanship. No captions, no text, no arrows, no diagrams, no glowing runes, no machinery, no science fiction. Proposed creature anatomy.
